title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is an arbitrary base scheme, and 2 is not assumed invertible. M is a rank-4 Azumaya algebra over O_S, locally End(V) for a rank-2 bundle V. G = M^* (a form of GL_2), and PG = G/G_m (a form of PGL_2). The Lie algebra of PG is M/O_S, which the next page calls PU.

The problem it serves. This belongs to the 'loop equation' section of the 'Longue Marche' continuation. That section studies the PGL_2-valued relations among the generators rho, sigma and the regular unipotent elements eps_0 = sigma^{-1} rho and eps_1 = rho sigma^{-1}. On the previous page Grothendieck noticed an apparent contradiction between two facts:
- Regular unipotents: (47) Unip.reg(G) modulo the group scheme mu'_{2,S} = {lambda : lambda^2 = 1, 2 lambda = 2} is isomorphic to Unip.reg(PG). So the map on regular unipotents is not injective.
- Borels: there is a bijection Borels(G) -> Borels(PG), and with it a bijection between unipotent one-parameter subgroups of G and of PG.

What this page does.
1. He first suspects the trouble lies in identifying the two sets of one-parameter subgroups via u in Gamma(M^*) with u N~ u^{-1} = mu N + lambda (crossed out; 'not so trivial'). He then locates the real difficulty elsewhere.
2. On G, a regular unipotent section eps = 1 + N canonically defines a parametrized one-parameter subgroup eps(t) = 1 + tN, a map G_a -> G. On PG, a regular unipotent section does not determine one.
3. Proof. Take lambda = 1 + nu with lambda^2 = 1 and 2 lambda = 2; equivalently nu^2 = 0 and 2 nu = 0. Such nu can be nonzero over non-reduced bases of residue characteristic 2.
   - Then eps' = lambda eps = 1 + N', with N' = (1+nu)N + nu.
   - N' is again nilpotent: N'^2 = (1+nu)^2 N^2 + 2 nu (1+nu) N + nu^2 = 0.
   - eps and eps' have the same image in PG, so the induced maps G_a -> G -> PG agree at t = 1.
   - Their derivatives at 0 are the maps O_S -> M -> M/O_S sending 1 to N~ and N~' = (1+nu) N~ respectively (the image of nu in M/O_S is 0).
   - Since N~ is a nowhere-vanishing section of the locally free M/O_S, nu N~ = 0 forces nu = 0.
   - Hence the two parametrized subgroups differ as soon as lambda is not 1.
4. Conclusion (next page). In the loop-equation data in PG one must give, besides rho~ and sigma~, parametrized one-parameter subgroups eps~_0, eps~_1 : G_a -> PG with eps~_1 = rho(eps~_0) = sigma(eps~_0). Equivalently one gives a regular unipotent lift eps_0 of eps~_0 to G, a lift that is not a priori unique.
errors: No mathematical error. The non-injectivity is genuine only over bases where 2 is not invertible and O_S has nilpotents (nu^2 = 0, 2 nu = 0, nu nonzero). Over Z[1/2], or over reduced bases, mu'_2 is trivial and the issue disappears. Grothendieck states the condition as 'des que nu != 0', which is correct.

The step 'nu N~ = 0 implies nu = 0' uses the fact that N~ is nowhere vanishing in a locally free quotient, so that O_S . N~ is locally a direct summand. This holds because a regular nilpotent N is nowhere a scalar mod m_s. Grothendieck asserts this without detail on the next page.

ideas.what: The finite flat group scheme mu'_2 = {lambda : lambda^2 = 1, 2 lambda = 2} (the stabilizer of the regular-unipotent locus under central scaling) and the identification Unip.reg(G)/mu'_2 = Unip.reg(PG) over an arbitrary base
ideas.modern_name: Center action on the regular unipotent locus; a subgroup scheme of mu_2 that is trivial over Z[1/2] and all of mu_2 in characteristic 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group-scheme considerations (SGA3 style); no specific attribution

ideas.what: Over PG a regular unipotent section does not determine a parametrized G_a-subgroup; the obstruction is detected by derivatives at the origin in Lie(PG) = M/O_S
ideas.modern_name: Failure of a unique 'exponential' / one-parameter subgroup through a unipotent element in bad characteristic over non-reduced bases
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore on unipotent elements in bad characteristic (e.g. work on Springer isomorphisms and exponentials)

ideas.what: Refinement of the PGL_2 'loop equation' data: include parametrized one-parameter subgroups eps~_0, eps~_1 (equivalently unipotent lifts to G) in addition to rho, sigma
ideas.modern_name: Rigidifying data for PGL_2-representations of the braid/Teichmuller-type relations over Z

missed.claim: The page shows Grothendieck treating the PGL_2 version of his loop equations over arbitrary bases, including characteristic 2 and non-reduced bases. To make the moduli problem well-behaved over Z he finds he must rigidify by adding parametrized G_a-subgroups (unipotent lifts). This is a technical detail of an unpublished project rather than a new theorem.
missed.quote: il faut considérer que l'on se donne dans PG, non seulement rho~ et sigma~ ... mais aussi des 'sous-groupes à 1 paramètre' (paramétrés)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' and the arithmetic, over-Z PGL_2 representation spaces of braid/mapping-class-type relations. It is of minor independent interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine group-scheme check: non-uniqueness of one-parameter subgroups through unipotents of PGL_2 in characteristic 2 over non-reduced bases. Its main interest is documenting how Grothendieck rigidified his loop-equation data; it contains no new result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'sections unipotentes singulières' should read 'sections unipotentes régulières' (both occurrences: 'rigulières').
'G_0 -> G -> PG' should read 'G_a -> G -> PG'.
'M/O_S ≃ PV' is likely 'M/O_S ≃ PU' (Lie algebra notation, consistent with the next page).
'(ses restrictions sur S)' is plausibly '(ni ses restrictions aux S')'; this is uncertain.
Previous page 'M'_{2,S}' is almost certainly 'mu'_{2,S}' (the group scheme defined by lambda^2 = 1, 2 lambda = 2).

First line 'mais Se marches pour des PG' is uncertain; it plausibly reads something like 'mais si on cherche pour des PG, c'est-à-dire ...'. 'pas puis trivial' is likely 'pas si trivial' or 'pas plus trivial'.
Inserted '{+λ≠1 i.e.+}' is written above 'si ν≠0'; it is consistent with the text.
